# S69 — Open slicer tui from the Roadmap with O

On the Roadmap, `O` hands the terminal to `slicer tui --root PROJECT_PATH` for the edits ork does not have, and ork re-reads the project when slicer's TUI exits. The key is `O`, decided by the owner on 2026-10-31.

## Why

`adj 11` (`ui.slicer-tui`, decided 2026-10-20, option `both`): common edits (reorder, park, start) are ork's own, and one key opens slicer's TUI for the rest. Moved to v1.1 on 2026-10-29 by `adj 173` (`scope.v1-ork-edits`, include). Key `O`: owner, 2026-10-31. The owner's earlier proviso ("`O` is proposed until the owner confirms") is closed by that answer.

Checked today:

- The invocation is `slicer tui [--root ROOT]` (`slicer tui --help`: `usage: slicer tui [-h] [--root ROOT]`, `--root ROOT  project root (default: discovered from the working directory)`). `ui` is the second name (`../slicer/docs/commands.md:97`, previously cited at `:91`). `../slicer/docs/tui.md` does not mention `--root`; the CLI help is the source for the form.
- Bubble Tea v2: `func ExecProcess(c *exec.Cmd, fn ExecCallback) Cmd` pauses the program while the command runs and resumes after it exits; `ExecCallback` is `func(error) Msg` (`go -C . doc charm.land/bubbletea/v2 ExecProcess`). Nothing in `internal/` uses it yet (`rg ExecProcess internal` is empty).
- ork's slicer calls go through `slicercli.Client`, whose binary is the name `slicer` on PATH when `Bin` is empty (`internal/slicercli/slicercli.go:16-23`). `cmd/ork/main.go` never sets `Tools.Slicer`. This slice therefore reads the binary from a new `tui.Config.SlicerBin` that defaults to `slicer`, and `cmd/ork/main.go` is not changed.

E-class: no. The slice touches `internal/tui` and `docs/dashboard.md` only. It needs no daemon call, no `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or `cmd` change, so it pairs with an engine-class slice. If the implementer finds that `cmd/ork/main.go` must change, stop and report: the pair plan depends on this.

What the TUI does on return (S69 had not said): it re-reads the selected project's snapshot, with the daemon's refresh when a daemon is connected, through `fetch(name, true)` (`internal/tui/model.go:307-322`), as the note and filing actions do after they write (`internal/tui/compose.go:141`, `:235`). The Roadmap list, the counts and readiness then show slicer's edits. A Waves plan is read when Waves opens, so it is not touched; an open Roadmap item pane would be stale, so the key is refused while one is open.

## Failing tests

In `internal/tui/slicertui_test.go`:

- `TestOpenSlicerTuiRunsSlicerTuiWithTheProjectRoot`: on the Roadmap with a loaded project, `O` calls `Config.Exec` once with a command whose `Args` are `[SlicerBin, "tui", "--root", PROJECT_PATH]` and returns a non-nil command. Fails first: the key is unbound.
- `TestOpenSlicerTuiIsRefusedOffTheRoadmap`: on the Overview, Waves, Questions and Decisions, with no project selected ("Needs you" or "Running"), with help open, with the Roadmap item pane open, with the matrix pane open, and for a project with no `.slicer/` folder or an unavailable project, `O` calls nothing; where the refusal has a status line it says why (for example `Select a project to open slicer tui`).
- `TestOpenSlicerTuiNeedsNoDaemon`: with `Config.Live` nil the key still runs.
- `TestDashboardRefreshesAfterSlicerTuiExits`: delivering the done message with a nil error makes the model fetch the project again (the fake source sees a second snapshot read) and clears the status line.
- `TestSlicerTuiExitErrorShowsOnTheStatusLine`: the done message with an error shows `slicer tui: ` plus the error text on the status line and still re-reads the project.
- `TestMissingSlicerShowsErrorAndDoesNotPanic`: with `SlicerBin` set to a name that is not on PATH, `O` returns no process command, sets a status line that names the binary, and does not call `Exec`. (The check is `exec.LookPath`; the tests that need a binary that exists pass `os.Args[0]`.)
- In `internal/tui/hint_test.go` style, `TestHintBarOffersSlicerTuiOnTheRoadmap`: the Roadmap hint line and the `?` help list `O slicer tui` when the key can act, and not elsewhere; on a narrow hint line `O slicer tui` drops with `+ add project` and `n new slice`, before `N note` (the existing `TestRoadmapNoteHintDropsBeforeMatrix` stays green).

## Implement

1. Tests first, from the list above; watch each fail for its stated reason.
2. `Config` gets `SlicerBin string` (empty means `slicer`) and `Exec func(*exec.Cmd, tea.ExecCallback) tea.Cmd` (nil means `tea.ExecProcess`), so tests capture the command and call the callback by hand. Defaults are set beside the other `Config` defaults (`internal/tui/model.go:190-205`).
3. `internal/tui/slicertui.go`: `func (m *Model) openSlicerTui() tea.Cmd`. Refuse, in this order and with the status text in parentheses, when: the view is not the Roadmap (`slicer tui opens from the Roadmap`); no project is selected (`Select a project to open slicer tui`); help is open (`Close help to open slicer tui`); the project is unavailable or has no `.slicer/` folder (`Project unavailable; cannot open slicer tui`); the matrix pane is open (no text, as `composeRefusal` does at `internal/tui/compose.go:47`); the Roadmap item pane is open (`Close the pane to open slicer tui`). Then `exec.LookPath(bin)`; on error set `slicer tui: ` plus the error and return nil. Otherwise build `exec.Command(bin, "tui", "--root", path)` and return `m.cfg.Exec(cmd, func(err error) tea.Msg { return slicerTuiDoneMsg{project: name, err: err} })`. Set no `Dir` and no `Env`.
4. `Update`: on `slicerTuiDoneMsg`, set the status line (error text, or empty) and return `m.fetch(msg.project, true)`. `fetch` returns nil when a read of that project is already in flight; the next poll then catches up.
5. `keys.go` and `view.go`: the binding (`O`, `shift+o`; help `O` / `open slicer tui (Roadmap)`), a drop tier equal to `dropAdd` and `dropNew` (so it drops first), the hint entry offered only when `openSlicerTui` would act, and the Roadmap help line. Check the help at 80x24 and 100x30 still shows `q quit; ? help`; if the added text does not fit on the existing Roadmap help line, give `O slicer tui` its own line only when the height allows, and tell the reviewer what was done.
6. `docs/dashboard.md`: the key, the refusal cases, that ork hands over the terminal (Bubble Tea `ExecProcess`) and re-reads the project on return, and the hint tier. State that slicer's TUI edits slicer's files itself and that ork writes nothing (`docs/boundaries.md`). Mark the wording *proposed* where no record decides it.
7. `go test ./internal/tui -update` only if a golden changes; review the diff.
8. `CHANGELOG.md`, last: add the entry at the bottom of the `## Unreleased` list (the parallel engine slice adds its entry at the top, so the two do not touch the same lines).

Do not touch `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon`, `cmd`, `internal/slicercli`, or the Waves and Overview code. UI slice: UI pass (r14).
